provenance.status: Every value in this rule was proposed to Max under decision d1902 for METHOD-CARD-BE, the Belgium port's method card, which is kept with the port's notes outside this repository. Each value is a proposal, not a settled method and not a statement of Belgian law, until that card records his ruling.
provenance.unit: One adult, that adult's co-resident partner and their co-resident dependent children. Every other adult in the household anchors a unit of their own. The unit is a co-residence stand-in for the persons a regional family-benefit income test and child count look at. rulespec-be at 632e1da1110ba881c68165e0cd3c2287b5b8ab08 takes those incomes and counts as supplied inputs and defines no membership.
provenance.entity: family_benefit_unit names the partition after the schemes it serves. axiom_rules_bindings.json gives it the engine name FamilyBenefitUnit, which no rulespec-be module declares at that commit, so no rule there computes on the unit. The regional family-benefit modules at that commit run on Child, so each unit fact reaches them as a person column.
provenance.max_age: 24. A person aged 24 or under can be a dependent child. Each of the four regional family-benefit eligibility modules at that commit closes its last age window below 25: flanders_family_benefits_student_age_limit_years, brussels_family_benefits_article_25_extended_age_limit_years, wallonia_family_benefits_extended_age_years and german_speaking_community_family_benefits_final_age_cap_years are each 25 and each is read with a strict comparison. Below that, the Walloon module also entitles a person under 21, with no study test, when wallonia_family_benefits_no_government_obstacle_applies holds. So every person those modules can entitle on age sits in a unit with the adults they live with. Two Flemish inputs reach past the limit (the month of the 25th birthday and a pre-1987 transition); a person they entitle at 25 or over heads their own unit. The limit decides no entitlement; the modules do.
provenance.financial_independence: None. An hours test needs a Belgian threshold, and no source read for this declaration gives one. Without a test the constructor reads no usual weekly hours. A working person aged 24 or under who lives with a parent stays in the parent's unit, and the modules decide whether that person is entitled.
provenance.parent_independence_min_age: None, the constructor's default. A parent of a co-resident child anchors a unit at any age, so a minor parent and that parent's child form a unit apart from the minor's own parents.
provenance.unparented_child: reference_person_unit. A person aged 24 or under who has no co-resident parent, no partner and no co-resident child, and who is not the household's reference person, joins the unit that holds the reference person, so a child raised by a grandparent or another adult sits in a unit with an adult. This is an assumption. Its one source covers the German-speaking Community only: article 28 of the decree of 23 April 2018, as published in the Moniteur belge of 12 June 2018 and held in the rulespec-be corpus at that commit (later amendments were not read), names the person who actually raises the child when no parent shares the child's domicile, and presumes that the adults who share that domicile do. That article picks a recipient, not a unit, and does not single out the reference person. A flatmate or lodger aged 24 or under lands in the reference person's unit too: a disclosed approximation, because one policy covers every age.
provenance.split_parents: first_parent_unit. A child whose two co-resident parents are not partners of each other joins parent 1's unit; the other value refuses the whole frame. A partition holds each child once, so it cannot give one child a place in two families, and flanders_family_benefits_equal_shared_housing stays a separate input.
provenance.refuse_dependent_reference_person: false. A reference person aged 24 or under with no co-resident parent anchors a unit. True would refuse any frame that holds such a person.
provenance.head: The unit's head is a construction label: the household reference person when that person is an adult of the unit, otherwise the older adult. This rule names no allocataire and no payee.
provenance.donor_pointers: Membership is only as good as the donor's pointers. A cohabiting couple with no partner pointer reads as two units: their child joins parent 1's unit, that unit reads as a single parent's, and parent 2 sits outside it. A partner or parent who lives elsewhere is not seen at all.
provenance.not_expressed: The constructor reads age, the partner and parent pointers and the household reference person. It reads no legal marital status, no enrolment, no income, no court designation and nobody outside the household. The partner pointer covers spouses and cohabiting partners alike. Whether an income test sums over this unit's adults, over all its members or over the household is decided where the income node is declared, not here.
